newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Autoliv profits boosted by acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Autoliv profits boosted by acquisitions.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv AB Thursday reported a 13 percent rise in 1996 profits, saying the negative effects of a weaker crown were overcome by the positive effects of acquisitions.
Autoliv posted a profit of 1.15 billion crowns ($159 million) as sales in the year to Dec. 31 rose 14 percent to 11.6 billion crowns ($1.6 billion).

Analysts said the result was much in line with market expectations and all eyes were on the company's soon-to-be-finalised merger with the automotive component unit of Morton International Inc. The deal with Chicago-based Morton, announced in September, will create one of the world's largest makers of airbags.

"The improvement was due largely to a higher degree of integration in operations and continued cost cutting," Autoliv said in a statement. "A negative effect of a stronger Swedish crown was outweighed by the positive effect from a company acquisition," it added. "Prices have continued to fall."

"If you take into account a non-recurring cost in the fourth quarter (of 10 million crowns, or $1.38 million) then the result was exactly in line with market expectations," analyst Jan Dworsky of Fiba told Reuters.

A company spokesman said the acquisition of two Swedish seat component companies -- now called Autoliv Hammarverken and Autoliv Mekan -- and French steering wheel company, Isodelta, helped the 1996 results.

Sales of airbags rose by 13 percent to 5.5 billion crowns ($759 million) while the sale of seat belts rose by 15 percent to 6.1 billion crowns ($841 million). Fourth-quarter sales rose 26 percent from a year ago.
Autoliv said the increase in sales outperformed growth in the most important market -- the manufacture of light vehicles in Europe -- which rose an estimated 3 percent in 1996.
But analysts said the market had limited interest in Autoliv's 1996 earnings and the focus was on the merger with Morton, for which a prospectus will be released in March.
A spokesman said the deal could be finalised in March or April. The new company, to be called Autoliv Inc., will have sales of $3 billion and a staff of 15,000 in Europe, Japan and the United States.
